text:
Kaedan Korczak came to Pittsburgh from Vegas with a reputation built on defending, and the twist is that his points have arrived first. He has 12 assists in 24 games, already most of last season's 16 in 78, on 18 minutes a night, and he still hasn't scored.

Some of that is real. The Penguins win 55.6% of the expected goals (chance quality) at five on five with him out there, nearly five points better than without him. Evolving-Hockey had him 41st of 215 defensemen last season at 1.6 wins above replacement, almost all of it from even-strength defense, with opponents' chances shrinking at a 97th-percentile rate when he was on.

Some of it won't hold. His 1.66 points per 60 sit well above our talent range of 0.82 to 1.32, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking flags the weakness: only 29% of his exits keep the puck, so expect clears off the glass. Pittsburgh has won two of its last ten. Korczak isn't the problem. He's the defenseman to watch when the forecheck comes.
headline: Korczak's assists outrun his game
